transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But before I answer further, let me thank you for moderating.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank the University of Miami for hosting us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I know the president will join me in welcoming all of Florida to this debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ve been through the roughest weeks anybody could imagine.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Our hearts go out to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we admire your pluck and perseverance.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I can make American safer than President Bush has made us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I believe President Bush and I both love our country equally.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we just have a different set of convictions about how you make America safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe America is safest and strongest when we are leading the world and we are leading strong alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ll never give a veto to any country over our security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I also know how to lead those alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president has left them in shatters across the globe, and we’re now 90 percent of the casualties in Iraq and 90 percent of the costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s wrong, and I think we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a better plan for homeland security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a better plan to be able to fight the war on terror by strengthening our military, strengthening our intelligence, by going after the financing more authoritatively, by doing what we need to do to rebuild the alliances, by reaching out to the Muslim world, which the president has almost not done, and beginning to isolate the radical Islamic Muslims, not have them isolate the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I know I can do a better job in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan to have a summit with all of the allies, something this president has not yet achieved, not yet been able to do to bring people to the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can do a better job of training the Iraqi forces to defend themselves, and I know that we can do a better job of preparing for elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: All of these, and especially homeland security, which we’ll talk about a little bit later.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I, too, thank the University of Miami, and say our prayers are with the good people of this state, who’ve suffered a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: September the 11th changed how America must look at the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And since that day, our nation has been on a multi-pronged strategy to keep our country safer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We pursued Al Qaida wherever Al Qaida tries to hide.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Seventy-five percent of known Al Qaida leaders have been brought to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The rest of them know we’re after them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve upheld the doctrine that said if you harbor a terrorist, you’re equally as guilty as the terrorist.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the Taliban are no longer in power.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ten million people have registered to vote in Afghanistan in the upcoming presidential election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In Iraq, we saw a threat, and we realized that after September the 11th, we must take threats seriously, before they fully materialize.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein now sits in a prison cell.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: America and the world are safer for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We continue to pursue our policy of disrupting those who proliferate weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Libya has disarmed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The A.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Khan network has been brought to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, as well, we’re pursuing a strategy of freedom around the world, because I understand free nations will reject terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Free nations will answer the hopes and aspirations of their people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Free nations will help us achieve the peace we all want.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t believe it’s going to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe I’m going to win, because the American people know I know how to lead.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve shown the American people I know how to lead.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have — I understand everybody in this country doesn’t agree with the decisions I’ve made.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I made some tough decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But people know where I stand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People out there listening know what I believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s how best it is to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This nation of ours has got a solemn duty to defeat this ideology of hate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a group of killers who will not only kill here, but kill children in Russia, that’ll attack unmercifully in Iraq, hoping to shake our will.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a duty to defeat this enemy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have a duty to protect our children and grandchildren.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The best way to defeat them is to never waver, to be strong, to use every asset at our disposal, is to constantly stay on the offensive and, at the same time, spread liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what people are seeing now is happening in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ten million citizens have registered to vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a phenomenal statistic.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That if given a chance to be free, they will show up at the polls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Forty-one percent of those 10 million are women.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In Iraq, no doubt about it, it’s tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s hard work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s incredibly hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know why?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because an enemy realizes the stakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The enemy understands a free Iraq will be a major defeat in their ideology of hatred.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why they’re fighting so vociferously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They showed up in Afghanistan when they were there, because they tried to beat us and they didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they’re showing up in Iraq for the same reason.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re trying to defeat us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if we lose our will, we lose.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if we remain strong and resolute, we will defeat this enemy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe in being strong and resolute and determined.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I will hunt down and kill the terrorists, wherever they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to be smart, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And smart means not diverting your attention from the real war on terror in Afghanistan against Osama bin Laden and taking if off to Iraq where the 9/11 Commission confirms there was no connection to 9/11 itself and Saddam Hussein, and where the reason for going to war was weapons of mass destruction, not the removal of Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president has made, I regret to say, a colossal error of judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And judgment is what we look for in the president of the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud that important military figures who are supporting me in this race: former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff John Shalikashvili; just yesterday, General Eisenhower’s son, General John Eisenhower, endorsed me; General Admiral William Crown; General Tony McBeak, who ran the Air Force war so effectively for his father — all believe I would make a stronger commander in chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And they believe it because they know I would not take my eye off of the goal: Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, he escaped in the mountains of Tora Bora.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We had him surrounded.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we didn’t use American forces, the best trained in the world, to go kill him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president relied on Afghan warlords and he outsourced that job too.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, where do you want me to begin?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: First of all, he made the misjudgment of saying to America that he was going to build a true alliance, that he would exhaust the remedies of the United Nations and go through the inspections.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In fact, he first didn’t even want to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And it wasn’t until former Secretary of State Jim Baker and General Scowcroft and others pushed publicly and said you’ve got to go to the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: , that the president finally changed his mind — his campaign has a word for that — and went to the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, once there, we could have continued those inspections.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We had Saddam Hussein trapped.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He also promised America that he would go to war as a last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Those words mean something to me, as somebody who has been in combat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: “Last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” You’ve got to be able to look in the eyes of families and say to those parents, “I tried to do everything in my power to prevent the loss of your son and daughter.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” I don’t believe the United States did that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we pushed our allies aside.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And so, today, we are 90 percent of the casualties and 90 percent of the cost: $200 billion — $200 billion that could have been used for health care, for schools, for construction, for prescription drugs for seniors, and it’s in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And Iraq is not even the center of the focus of the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The center is Afghanistan, where, incidentally, there were more Americans killed last year than the year before; where the opium production is 75 percent of the world’s opium production; where 40 to 60 percent of the economy of Afghanistan is based on opium; where the elections have been postponed three times.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president moved the troops, so he’s got 10 times the number of troops in Iraq than he has in Afghanistan, where Osama bin Laden is.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Does that mean that Saddam Hussein was 10 times more important than Osama bin Laden — than, excuse me, Saddam Hussein more important than Osama bin Laden?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent looked at the same intelligence I looked at and declared in 2002 that Saddam Hussein was a grave threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He also said in December of 2003 that anyone who doubts that the world is safer without Saddam Hussein does not have the judgment to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I agree with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The world is better off without Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was hoping diplomacy would work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I understand the serious consequences of committing our troops into harm’s way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the hardest decision a president makes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I went to the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t need anybody to tell me to go to the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I decided to go there myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I went there hoping that, once and for all, the free world would act in concert to get Saddam Hussein to listen to our demands.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They passed the resolution that said, “Disclose, disarm, or face serious consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” I believe, when an international body speaks, it must mean what it says.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein had no intention of disarming.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Why should he?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He had 16 other resolutions and nothing took place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, my opponent talks about inspectors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The facts are that he was systematically deceiving the inspectors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t going to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s kind of a pre-September 10th mentality, the hope that somehow resolutions and failed inspections would make this world a more peaceful place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He was hoping we’d turn away.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there was fortunately others beside myself who believed that we ought to take action.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The world is safer without Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Jim, we’ve got the capability of doing both.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, this is a global effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re facing a group of folks who have such hatred in their heart, they’ll strike anywhere, with any means.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why it’s essential that we have strong alliances, and we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why it’s essential that we make sure that we keep weapons of mass destruction out of the hands of people like Al Qaida, which we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But to say that there’s only one focus on the war on terror doesn’t really understand the nature of the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’re after Saddam Hussein — I mean bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s isolated.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Seventy-five percent of his people have been brought to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The killer — the mastermind of the September 11th attacks, Khalid Sheik Mohammed, is in prison.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re making progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the front on this war is more than just one place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Philippines — we’ve got help — we’re helping them there to bring — to bring Al Qaida affiliates to justice there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, of course, Iraq is a central part in the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why Zarqawi and his people are trying to fight us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Their hope is that we grow weary and we leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The biggest disaster that could happen is that we not succeed in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a plan to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the main reason we’ll succeed is because the Iraqis want to be free.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I had the honor of visiting with Prime Minister Allawi.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s a strong, courageous leader.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He believes in the freedom of the Iraqi people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He doesn’t want U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: leadership, however, to send mixed signals, to not stand with the Iraqi people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He believes, like I believe, that the Iraqis are ready to fight for their own freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They just need the help to be trained.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There will be elections in January.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re spending reconstruction money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And our alliance is strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the plan for victory.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And when Iraq if free, America will be more secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president just talked about Iraq as a center of the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Iraq was not even close to the center of the war on terror before the president invaded it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president made the judgment to divert forces from under General Tommy Franks from Afghanistan before the Congress even approved it to begin to prepare to go to war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And he rushed the war in Iraq without a plan to win the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, that is not the judgment that a president of the United States ought to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You don’t take America to war unless have the plan to win the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You don’t send troops to war without the body armor that they need.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met kids in Ohio, parents in Wisconsin places, Iowa, where they’re going out on the Internet to get the state-of-the-art body gear to send to their kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Some of them got it for a birthday present.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Humvees — 10,000 out of 12,000 Humvees that are over there aren’t armored.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And you go visit some of those kids in the hospitals today who were maimed because they don’t have the armament.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president just — I don’t know if he sees what’s really happened over there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But it’s getting worse by the day.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: More soldiers killed in June than before.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: More in July than June.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: More in August than July.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: More in September than in August.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And now we see beheadings.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we got weapons of mass destruction crossing the border every single day, and they’re blowing people up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we don’t have enough troops there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Can I respond to that?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, what my opponent wants you to forget is that he voted to authorize the use of force and now says it’s the wrong war at the wrong time at the wrong place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t see how you can lead this country to succeed in Iraq if you say wrong war, wrong time, wrong place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What message does that send our troops?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What message does that send to our allies?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What message does that send the Iraqis?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, the way to win this is to be steadfast and resolved and to follow through on the plan that I’ve just outlined.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we have to be steadfast and resolved, and I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I will succeed for those troops, now that we’re there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can’t leave a failed Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But that doesn’t mean it wasn’t a mistake of judgment to go there and take the focus off of Osama bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It was.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, we can succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t believe this president can.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think we need a president who has the credibility to bring the allies back to the table and to do what’s necessary to make it so America isn’t doing this alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Jim, let me tell you exactly what I’ll do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And there are a long list of thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: First of all, what kind of mixed message does it send when you have $500 million going over to Iraq to put police officers in the streets of Iraq, and the president is cutting the COPS program in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What kind of message does it send to be sending money to open firehouses in Iraq, but we’re shutting firehouses who are the first- responders here in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president hasn’t put one nickel, not one nickel into the effort to fix some of our tunnels and bridges and most exposed subway systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why they had to close down the subway in New York when the Republican Convention was there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We hadn’t done the work that ought to be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president — 95 percent of the containers that come into the ports, right here in Florida, are not inspected.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Civilians get onto aircraft, and their luggage is X-rayed, but the cargo hold is not X- rayed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Does that make you feel safer in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This president thought it was more important to give the wealthiest people in America a tax cut rather than invest in homeland security.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Those aren’t my values.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe in protecting America first.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And long before President Bush and I get a tax cut — and that’s who gets it — long before we do, I’m going to invest in homeland security and I’m going to make sure we’re not cutting COPS programs in America and we’re fully staffed in our firehouses and that we protect the nuclear and chemical plants.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president also unfortunately gave in to the chemical industry, which didn’t want to do some of the things necessary to strengthen our chemical plant exposure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And there’s an enormous undone job to protect the loose nuclear materials in the world that are able to get to terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s a whole other subject, but I see we still have a little bit more time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Let me just quickly say, at the current pace, the president will not secure the loose material in the Soviet Union — former Soviet Union for 13 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to do it in four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to keep it out of the hands of terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we want to get to how he’s going to pay for all these promises.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s like a huge tax gap.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Anyway, that’s for another debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My administration has tripled the amount of money we’re spending on homeland security to $30 billion a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My administration worked with the Congress to create the Department of Homeland Security so we could better coordinate our borders and ports.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got 1,000 extra border patrol on the southern border; want 1,000 on the northern border.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re modernizing our borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We spent $3.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 1 billion for fire and police, $3.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 1 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing our duty to provide the funding.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the best way to protect this homeland is to stay on the offense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, we have to be right 100 percent of the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the enemy only has to be right once to hurt us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a lot of good people working hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, we’ve also changed the culture of the FBI to have counterterrorism as its number one priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re communicating better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to reform our intelligence services to make sure that we get the best intelligence possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Patriot Act is vital — is vital that the Congress renew the Patriot Act which enables our law enforcement to disrupt terror cells.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But again, I repeat to my fellow citizens, the best way to protection is to stay on the offense.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president just said the FBI had changed its culture.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We just read on the front pages of America’s papers that there are over 100,000 hours of tapes, unlistened to.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: On one of those tapes may be the enemy being right the next time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the test is not whether you’re spending more money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The test is, are you doing everything possible to make America safe?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t need that tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: America needed to be safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’re doing everything we can to protect America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wake up every day thinking about how best to protect America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s my job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I work with Director Mueller of the FBI; comes in my office when I’m in Washington every morning, talking about how to protect us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a lot of really good people working hard to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s hard work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But, again, I want to tell the American people, we’re doing everything we can at home, but you better have a president who chases these terrorists down and bring them to justice before they hurt us again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me first tell you that the best way for Iraq to be safe and secure is for Iraqi citizens to be trained to do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got 100,000 trained now, 125,000 by the end of this year, 200,000 by the end of next year.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is the best way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll never succeed in Iraq if the Iraqi citizens do not want to take matters into their own hands to protect themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe they want to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Prime Minister Allawi believes they want to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so the best indication about when we can bring our troops home — which I really want to do, but I don’t want to do so for the sake of bringing them home; I want to do so because we’ve achieved an objective — is to see the Iraqis perform and to see the Iraqis step up and take responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so, the answer to your question is: When our general is on the ground and Ambassador Negroponte tells me that Iraq is ready to defend herself from these terrorists, that elections will have been held by then, that their stability and that they’re on their way to, you know, a nation that’s free; that’s when.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I hope it’s as soon as possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I know putting artificial deadlines won’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent at one time said, “Well, get me elected, I’ll have them out of there in six months.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” You can’t do that and expect to win the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My message to our troops is, “Thank you for what you’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re standing with you strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll give you all the equipment you need.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll get you home as soon as the mission’s done, because this is a vital mission.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” A free Iraq will be an ally in the war on terror, and that’s essential.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A free Iraq will set a powerful example in the part of the world that is desperate for freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A free Iraq will help secure Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A free Iraq will enforce the hopes and aspirations of the reformers in places like Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A free Iraq is essential for the security of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: My message to the troops is also: Thank you for what they’re doing, but it’s also help is on the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe those troops deserve better than what they are getting today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You know, it’s interesting.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: When I was in a rope line just the other day, coming out here from Wisconsin, a couple of young returnees were in the line, one active duty, one from the Guard.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And they both looked at me and said: We need you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to help us over there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now I believe there’s a better way to do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You know, the president’s father did not go into Iraq, into Baghdad, beyond Basra.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the reason he didn’t is, he said — he wrote in his book — because there was no viable exit strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And he said our troops would be occupiers in a bitterly hostile land.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly where we find ourselves today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: There’s a sense of American occupation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The only building that was guarded when the troops when into Baghdad was the oil ministry.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t guard the nuclear facilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t guard the foreign office, where you might have found information about weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t guard the borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Almost every step of the way, our troops have been left on these extraordinarily difficult missions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to go out on one of those missions when you don’t know what’s around the corner.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I believe our troops need other allies helping.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to hold that summit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I will bring fresh credibility, a new start, and we will get the job done right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s worthy for a follow-up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent says help is on the way, but what kind of message does it say to our troops in harm’s way, “wrong war, wrong place, wrong time”?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not a message a commander in chief gives, or this is a “great diversion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” As well, help is on the way, but it’s certainly hard to tell it when he voted against the $87-billion supplemental to provide equipment for our troops, and then said he actually did vote for it before he voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not what a commander in chief does when you’re trying to lead troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, when I talked about the $87 billion, I made a mistake in how I talk about the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But the president made a mistake in invading Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Which is worse?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe that when you know something’s going wrong, you make it right.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I learned in Vietnam.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: When I came back from that war I saw that it was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Some people don’t like the fact that I stood up to say no, but I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I did with that vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to lead those troops to victory.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: No, and they don’t have to, providing we have the leadership that we put — that I’m offering.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we have to win this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president and I have always agreed on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And from the beginning, I did vote to give the authority, because I thought Saddam Hussein was a threat, and I did accept that intelligence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I also laid out a very strict series of things we needed to do in order to proceed from a position of strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Then the president, in fact, promised them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He went to Cincinnati and he gave a speech in which he said, “We will plan carefully.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We will proceed cautiously.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We will not make war inevitable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We will go with our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” He didn’t do any of those things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t do the planning.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They left the planning of the State Department in the State Department desks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They avoided even the advice of their own general.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: General Shinsheki, the Army chief of staff, said you’re going to need several hundred thousand troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Instead of listening to him, they retired him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The terrorism czar, who has worked for every president since Ronald Reagan, said, “Invading Iraq in response to 9/11 would be like Franklin Roosevelt invading Mexico in response to Pearl Harbor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s what we have here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And what we need now is a president who understands how to bring these other countries together to recognize their stakes in this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They do have stakes in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve always had stakes in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The Arab countries have a stake in not having a civil war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The European countries have a stake in not having total disorder on their doorstep.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But this president hasn’t even held the kind of statesman-like summits that pull people together and get them to invest in those states.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In fact, he’s done the opposite.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He pushed them away.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: When the Secretary General Kofi Annan offered the United Nations, he said, “No, no, we’ll go do this alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” To save for Halliburton the spoils of the war, they actually issued a memorandum from the Defense Department saying, “If you weren’t with us in the war, don’t bother applying for any construction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s not a way to invite people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s totally absurd.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course, the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: was invited in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we support the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: efforts there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They pulled out after Sergio de Mello got killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But they’re now back in helping with elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent says we didn’t have any allies in this war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s he say to Tony Blair?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s he say to Alexander Kwasniewski of Poland?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t expect to build an alliance when you denigrate the contributions of those who are serving side by side with American troops in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Plus, he says the cornerstone of his plan to succeed in Iraq is to call upon nations to serve.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So what’s the message going to be: “Please join us in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For a grand diversion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Join us for a war that is the wrong war at the wrong place at the wrong time?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” I know how these people think.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I deal with them all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I sit down with the world leaders frequently and talk to them on the phone frequently.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re not going to follow somebody who says, “This is the wrong war at the wrong place at the wrong time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” They’re not going to follow somebody who says this is the wrong war at the wrong place at the wrong time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re not going to follow somebody whose core convictions keep changing because of politics in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And finally, he says we ought to have a summit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, there are summits being held.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Japan is going to have a summit for the donors; $14 billion pledged.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And Prime Minister Koizumi is going to call countries to account, to get them to contribute.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there’s going to be an Arab summit, of the neighborhood countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And Colin Powell helped set up that summit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The United Nations, Kofi Annan offered help after Baghdad fell.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we never picked him up on that and did what was necessary to transfer authority and to transfer reconstruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It was always American-run.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, when we went in, there were three countries: Great Britain, Australia and the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not a grand coalition.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, actually, he forgot Poland.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now there’s 30 nations involved, standing side by side with our American troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I honor their sacrifices.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t appreciate it when a candidate for president denigrates the contributions of these brave soldiers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You cannot lead the world if you do not honor the contributions of those who are with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He called them coerced and the bribed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not how you bring people together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our coalition is strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will remain strong, so long as I’m the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, what I said was that, because we achieved such a rapid victory, more of the Saddam loyalists were around.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we thought we’d whip more of them going in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But because Tommy Franks did such a great job in planning the operations, we moved rapidly, and a lot of the Baathists and Saddam loyalists laid down their arms and disappeared.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought they would stay and fight, but they didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now we’re fighting them now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s hard work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I understand how hard it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I get the casualty reports every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see on the TV screens how hard it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s necessary work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m optimistic.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See, I think you can be realistic and optimistic at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m optimistic we’ll achieve — I know we won’t achieve if we send mixed signals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know we’re not going to achieve our objective if we send mixed signals to our troops, our friends, the Iraqi citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a plan in place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The plan says there will be elections in January, and there will be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The plan says we’ll train Iraqi soldiers so they can do the hard work, and we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not only just America, but NATO is now helping, Jordan’s helping train police, UAE is helping train police.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve allocated $7 billion over the next months for reconstruction efforts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re making progress there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And our alliance is strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as I just told you, there’s going to be a summit of the Arab nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Japan will be hosting a summit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re making progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is hard work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is hard work to go from a tyranny to a democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s hard work to go from a place where people get their hands cut off, or executed, to a place where people are free.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s necessary work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And a free Iraq is going to make this world a more peaceful place.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What I think troubles a lot of people in our country is that the president has just sort of described one kind of mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But what he has said is that, even knowing there were no weapons of mass destruction, even knowing there was no imminent threat, even knowing there was no connection with Al Qaida, he would still have done everything the same way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Those are his words.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, I would not.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So what I’m trying to do is just talk the truth to the American people and to the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The truth is what good policy is based on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s what leadership is based on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president says that I’m denigrating these troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have nothing but respect for the British, Tony Blair, and for what they’ve been willing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But you can’t tell me that when the most troops any other country has on the ground is Great Britain, with 8,300, and below that the four others are below 4,000, and below that, there isn’t anybody out of the hundreds, that we have a genuine coalition to get this job done.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You can’t tell me that on the day that we went into that war and it started — it was principally the United States, the America and Great Britain and one or two others.

transcript_turns.text: Al Qaida attacked us.
