transcript_turns.text: And when we had Osama bin Laden cornered in the mountains of Tora Bora, 1,000 of his cohorts with him in those mountains.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: With the American military forces nearby and in the field, we didn’t use the best trained troops in the world to go kill the world’s number one criminal and terrorist.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They outsourced the job to Afghan warlords, who only a week earlier had been on the other side fighting against us, neither of whom trusted each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the enemy that attacked us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the enemy that was allowed to walk out of those mountains.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the enemy that is now in 60 countries, with stronger recruits.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He also said Saddam Hussein would have been stronger.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That is just factually incorrect.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Two-thirds of the country was a no-fly zone when we started this war.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We would have had sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We would have had the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: inspectors.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein would have been continually weakening.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: If the president had shown the patience to go through another round of resolution, to sit down with those leaders, say, “What do you need, what do you need now, how much more will it take to get you to join us?

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” we’d be in a stronger place today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, of course I know Osama bin Laden attacked us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And secondly, to think that another round of resolutions would have caused Saddam Hussein to disarm, disclose, is ludicrous, in my judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It just shows a significant difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We tried diplomacy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We did our best.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He was hoping to turn a blind eye.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, yes, he would have been stronger had we not dealt with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He had the capability of making weapons, and he would have made weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thirty-five to forty countries in the world had a greater capability of making weapons at the moment the president invaded than Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And while he’s been diverted, with 9 out of 10 active duty divisions of our Army, either going to Iraq, coming back from Iraq, or getting ready to go, North Korea’s gotten nuclear weapons and the world is more dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Iran is moving toward nuclear weapons and the world is more dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Darfur has a genocide.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The world is more dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’d have made a better choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me — I’m not exactly sure what you mean, “passes the global test,” you take preemptive action if you pass a global test.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My attitude is you take preemptive action in order to protect the American people, that you act in order to make this country secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent talks about me not signing certain treaties.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you one thing I didn’t sign, and I think it shows the difference of our opinion — the difference of opinions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that is, I wouldn’t join the International Criminal Court.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a body based in The Hague where unaccountable judges and prosecutors can pull our troops or diplomats up for trial.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I wouldn’t join it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I understand that in certain capitals around the world that that wasn’t a popular move.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s the right move not to join a foreign court that could — where our people could be prosecuted.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent is for joining the International Criminal Court.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just think trying to be popular, kind of, in the global sense, if it’s not in our best interest makes no sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m interested in working with our nations and do a lot of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not going to make decisions that I think are wrong for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: North Korea, first, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me say — I certainly hope so.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Before I was sworn in, the policy of this government was to have bilateral negotiations with North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we signed an agreement with North Korea that my administration found out that was not being honored by the North Koreans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I decided that a better way to approach the issue was to get other nations involved, just besides us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in Crawford, Texas, Jiang Zemin and I agreed that the nuclear-weapons-free peninsula, Korean Peninsula, was in his interest and our interest and the world’s interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we began a new dialogue with North Korea, one that included not only the United States, but now China.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And China’s a got a lot of influence over North Korea, some ways more than we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As well, we included South Korea, Japan and Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So now there are five voices speaking to Kim Jong Il, not just one.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so if Kim Jong Il decides again to not honor an agreement, he’s not only doing injustice to America, he’d be doing injustice to China, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think this will work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to work if we open up a dialogue with Kim Jong Il.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thatâ€™s what he wants.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He wants to unravel the six- party talks, or the five-nation coalition that’s sending him a clear message.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On Iran, I hope we can do the same thing, continue to work with the world to convince the Iranian mullahs to abandon their nuclear ambitions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We worked very closely with the foreign ministers of France, Germany and Great Britain, who have been the folks delivering the message to the mullahs that if you expect to be part of the world of nations, get rid of your nuclear programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The IAEA is involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a special protocol recently been passed that allows for inspections.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope we can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a good strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: With respect to Iran, the British, French, and Germans were the ones who initiated an effort without the United States, regrettably, to begin to try to move to curb the nuclear possibilities in Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe we could have done better.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think the United States should have offered the opportunity to provide the nuclear fuel, test them, see whether or not they were actually looking for it for peaceful purposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: If they weren’t willing to work a deal, then we could have put sanctions together.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president did nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: With respect to North Korea, the real story: We had inspectors and television cameras in the nuclear reactor in North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Secretary Bill Perry negotiated that under President Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we knew where the fuel rods were.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we knew the limits on their nuclear power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Colin Powell, our secretary of state, announced one day that we were going to continue the dialog of working with the North Koreans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president reversed it publicly while the president of South Korea was here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the president of South Korea went back to South Korea bewildered and embarrassed because it went against his policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And for two years, this administration didn’t talk at all to North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: While they didn’t talk at all, the fuel rods came out, the inspectors were kicked out, the television cameras were kicked out.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And today, there are four to seven nuclear weapons in the hands of North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That happened on this president’s watch.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, that, I think, is one of the most serious, sort of, reversals or mixed messages that you could possibly send.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Right.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Both.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I want bilateral talks which put all of the issues, from the armistice of 1952, the economic issues, the human rights issues, the artillery disposal issues, the DMZ issues and the nuclear issues on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The minute we have bilateral talks, the six-party talks will unwind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly what Kim Jong Il wants.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, the breach on the agreement was not through plutonium.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The breach on the agreement is highly enriched uranium.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we caught him doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s where he was breaking the agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, he said — my opponent said where he worked to put sanctions on Iran — we’ve already sanctioned Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t sanction them any more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are sanctions in place on Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And finally, we were a party to the convention — to working with Germany, France and Great Britain to send their foreign ministers into Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ll tell you exactly why not, but I first want to say something about those sanctions on Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Only the United States put the sanctions on alone, and that’s exactly what I’m talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: In order for the sanctions to be effective, we should have been working with the British, French and Germans and other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the difference between the president and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And there, again, he sort of slid by the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, with respect to Darfur, yes, it is a genocide.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And months ago, many of us were pressing for action.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think the reason that we’re not saying send American troops in at this point is severalfold.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Number one, we can do this through the African Union, providing we give them the logistical support.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Right now all the president is providing is humanitarian support.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We need to do more than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got to have the logistical capacity to go in and stop the killing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And that’s going to require more than is on the table today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I also believe that it is — one of the reasons we can’t do it is we’re overextended.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Ask the people in the armed forces today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got Guards and Reserves who are doing double duties.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a backdoor draft taking place in America today: people with stop-loss programs where they’re told you can’t get out of the military; nine out of our 10 active duty divisions committed to Iraq one way or the other, either going, coming or preparing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: So this is the way the president has overextended the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s why, in my plan, I add two active duty divisions to the United States Army, not for Iraq, but for our general demands across the globe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I also intend to double the number of special forces so that we can do the job we need to do with respect fighting the terrorists around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And if we do that, then we have the ability to be able to respond more rapidly.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I’ll tell you this, as president, if it took American forces to some degree to coalesce the African Union, I’d be prepared to do it because we could never allow another Rwanda.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s a moral responsibility for us and the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Back to Iran, just for a second.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was not my administration that put the sanctions on Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That happened long before I arrived in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of Darfur, I agree it’s genocide.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And Colin Powell so stated.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have committed $200 million worth of aid.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re the leading donor in the world to help the suffering people there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will commit more over time to help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We were very much involved at the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: on the sanction policy of the Bashir government in the Sudan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Prior to Darfur, Ambassador Jack Danforth had been negotiating a north-south agreement that we would have hoped would have brought peace to the Sudan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I agree with my opponent that we shouldn’t be committing troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We ought to be working with the African Union to do so — precisely what we did in Liberia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We helped stabilize the situation with some troops, and when the African Union came, we moved them out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My hope is that the African Union moves rapidly to help save lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And fortunately the rainy season will be ending shortly, which will make it easier to get aid there and help the long-suffering people there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s a loaded question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I admire Senator Kerry’s service to our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I admire the fact that he is a great dad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate the fact that his daughters have been so kind to my daughters in what has been a pretty hard experience for, I guess, young girls, seeing their dads out there campaigning.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I admire the fact that he served for 20 years in the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Although I’m not so sure I admire the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I won’t hold it against him that he went to Yale.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s nothing wrong with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My concerns about the senator is that, in the course of this campaign, I’ve been listening very carefully to what he says, and he changes positions on the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He changes positions on something as fundamental as what you believe in your core, in your heart of hearts, is right in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You cannot lead if you send mixed messages.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mixed messages send the wrong signals to our troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mixed messages send the wrong signals to our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mixed messages send the wrong signals to the Iraqi citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s my biggest concern about my opponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I admire his service.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I just know how this world works, and that in the councils of government, there must be certainty from the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we change tactics when need to, but we never change our beliefs, the strategic beliefs that are necessary to protect this country in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I appreciate enormously the personal comments the president just made.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I share them with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think only if you’re doing this — and he’s done it more than I have in terms of the presidency — can you begin to get a sense of what it means to your families.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And it’s tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And so I acknowledge that his daughters — I’ve watched them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve chuckled a few times at some of their comments.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And…

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m trying to put a leash on them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, I know.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve learned not to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I have great respect and admiration for his wife.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I think she’s a terrific person…

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: … and a great first lady.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we do have differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to talk about a difference of character.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s my job or my business.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But let me talk about something that the president just sort of finished up with.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Maybe someone would call it a character trait, maybe somebody wouldn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But this issue of certainty.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s one thing to be certain, but you can be certain and be wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s another to be certain and be right, or to be certain and be moving in the right direction, or be certain about a principle and then learn new facts and take those new facts and put them to use in order to change and get your policy right.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: What I worry about with the president is that he’s not acknowledging what’s on the ground, he’s not acknowledging the realities of North Korea, he’s not acknowledging the truth of the science of stem-cell research or of global warming and other issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And certainty sometimes can get you in trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think — listen, I fully agree that one should shift tactics, and we will, in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our commanders have got all the flexibility to do what is necessary to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But what I won’t do is change my core values because of politics or because of pressure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it is one of the things I’ve learned in the White House, is that there’s enormous pressure on the president, and he cannot wilt under that pressure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Otherwise, the world won’t be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have no intention of wilting.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’ve never wilted in my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve never wavered in my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I know exactly what we need to do in Iraq, and my position has been consistent: Saddam Hussein is a threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: He needed to be disarmed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We needed to go to the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president needed the authority to use force in order to be able to get him to do something, because he never did it without the threat of force.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we didn’t need to rush to war without a plan to win the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: There’s some 600-plus tons of unsecured material still in the former Soviet Union and Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: At the rate that the president is currently securing it, it’ll take 13 years to get it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I did a lot of work on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I wrote a book about it several years ago — six, seven years ago — called “The New War,” which saw the difficulties of this international criminal network.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And back then, we intercepted a suitcase in a Middle Eastern country with nuclear materials in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And the black market sale price was about $250 million.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now, there are terrorists trying to get their hands on that stuff today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And this president, I regret to say, has secured less nuclear material in the last two years since 9/11 than we did in the two years preceding 9/11.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We have to do this job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And to do the job, you can’t cut the money for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president actually cut the money for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You have to put the money into it and the funding and the leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And part of that leadership is sending the right message to places like North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Right now the president is spending hundreds of millions of dollars to research bunker-busting nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The United States is pursuing a new set of nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t make sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: You talk about mixed messages.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We’re telling other people, “You can’t have nuclear weapons,” but we’re pursuing a new nuclear weapon that we might even contemplate using.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Not this president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to shut that program down, and we’re going to make it clear to the world we’re serious about containing nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to get the job of containing all of that nuclear material in Russia done in four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to build the strongest international network to prevent nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This is the scale of what President Kennedy set out to do with the nuclear test ban treaty.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s our generation’s equivalent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I intend to get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Actually, we’ve increased funding for dealing with nuclear proliferation about 35 percent since I’ve been the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we’ve set up what’s called the — well, first of all, I agree with my opponent that the biggest threat facing this country is weapons of mass destruction in the hands of a terrorist network.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why proliferation is one of the centerpieces of a multi-prong strategy to make the country safer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My administration started what’s called the Proliferation Security Initiative.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over 60 nations involved with disrupting the trans-shipment of information and/or weapons of mass destruction materials.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve been effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We busted the A.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Khan network.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This was a proliferator out of Pakistan that was selling secrets to places like North Korea and Libya.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We convinced Libya to disarm.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a central part of dealing with weapons of mass destruction and proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you another way to help protect America in the long run is to continue with missile defenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a robust research and development program that has been ongoing during my administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll be implementing a missile-defense system relatively quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that is another way to help deal with the threats that we face in the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My opponent opposed the missile defenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In the hands of a terrorist enemy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Weapons of mass destruction, nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But again, the test or the difference between us, the president has had four years to try to do something about it, and North Korea has got more weapons; Iran is moving towards weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And at his pace, it will take 13 years to secure those weapons in Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to do it in four years, and I’m going to immediately set out to have bilateral talks with North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Again, I can’t tell you how big a mistake I think that is, to have bilateral talks with North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s precisely what Kim Jong Il wants.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will cause the six-party talks to evaporate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will mean that China no longer is involved in convincing, along with us, for Kim Jong Il to get rid of his weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a big mistake to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We must have China’s leverage on Kim Jong Il, besides ourselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if you enter bilateral talks, they’ll be happy to walk away from the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’ll work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t think it’s OK, and said so publicly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that there needs to be checks and balances in a democracy, and made that very clear that by consolidating power in the central government, he’s sending a signal to the Western world and United States that perhaps he doesn’t believe in checks and balances, and I told him that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, he’s also a strong ally in the war on terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is — listen, they went through a horrible situation in Beslan, where these terrorists gunned down young school kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the nature of the enemy, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we need to be firm and resolved in bringing them to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s precisely what Vladimir Putin understands, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a good relation with Vladimir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s important that we do have a good relation, because that enables me to better comment to him, and to better to discuss with him, some of the decisions he makes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I found that, in this world, that it’s important to establish good personal relationships with people so that when you have disagreements, you’re able to disagree in a way that is effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’ve told him my opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I look forward to discussing it more with him, as time goes on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Russia is a country in transition.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vladimir is going to have to make some hard choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s very important for the American president, as well as other Western leaders, to remind him of the great benefits of democracy, that democracy will best help the people realize their hopes and aspirations and dreams.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I will continue working with him over the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just say quickly that I’ve had an extraordinary experience of watching up close and personal that transition in Russia, because I was there right after the transformation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I was probably one of the first senators, along with Senator Bob Smith of New Hampshire, a former senator, to go down into the KGB underneath Treblinka Square and see reams of files with names in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It sort of brought home the transition to democracy that Russia was trying to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I regret what’s happened in these past months.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I think it goes beyond just the response to terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Putin now controls all the television stations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: His political opposition is being put in jail.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s very important to the United States, obviously, to have a working relationship that is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: This is a very important country to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We want a partnership.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we always have to stand up for democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: As George Will said the other day, “Freedom on the march; not in Russia right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: ” Now, I’d like to come back for a quick moment, if I can, to that issue about China and the talks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Because that’s one of the most critical issues here: North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Just because the president says it can’t be done, that you’d lose China, doesn’t mean it can’t be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I mean, this is the president who said “There were weapons of mass destruction,” said “Mission accomplished,” said we could fight the war on the cheap — none of which were true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: We could have bilateral talks with Kim Jong Il.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we can get those weapons at the same time as we get China.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Because China has an interest in the outcome, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know my opinion on North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can’t say it any more plainly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Pardon me?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Oh, I’m a pretty calm guy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t take it personally.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, we looked at the same intelligence and came to the same conclusion: that Saddam Hussein was a grave threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t hold it against him that he said grave threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to go around the country saying he didn’t tell the truth, when he looked at the same intelligence I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It was a threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The issue is what you do about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: The president said he was going to build a true coalition, exhaust the remedies of the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: and go to war as a last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Those words really have to mean something.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And, unfortunately, he didn’t go to war as a last resort.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Now we have this incredible mess in Iraq — $200 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: It’s not what the American people thought they were getting when they voted.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim, very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much to the university, again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: My fellow Americans, as I’ve said at the very beginning of this debate, both President Bush and I love this country very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt, I think, about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But we have a different set of convictions about how we make our country stronger here at home and respected again in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I know that for many of you sitting at home, parents of kids in Iraq, you want to know who’s the person who could be a commander in chief who could get your kids home and get the job done and win the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And for all the rest of the parents in America who are wondering about their kids going to the school or anywhere else in the world, what kind of world they’re going to grow up in, let me look you in the eye and say to you: I defended this country as a young man in war, and I will defend it as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: But I have a difference with this president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe when we’re strongest when we reach out and lead the world and build strong alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan for Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe we can be successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m not talking about leaving.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I’m talking about winning.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And we need a fresh start, a new credibility, a president who can bring allies to our side.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I also have a plan to win the war on terror, funding homeland security, strengthening our military, cutting our finances, reaching out to the world, again building strong alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I believe America’s best days are ahead of us because I believe that the future belongs to freedom, not to fear.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: That’s the country that I’m going to fight for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And I ask you to give me the opportunity to make you proud.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: I ask you to give me the opportunity to lead this great nation, so that we can be stronger here at home, respected again in the world, and have responsible leadership that we deserve.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John Kerry
transcript_turns.text: And God bless America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much tonight, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Senator.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If America shows uncertainty or weakness in this decade, the world will drift toward tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not going to happen, so long as I’m your president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The next four years we will continue to strengthen our homeland defenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will strengthen our intelligence-gathering services.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will reform our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The military will be an all-volunteer army.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will continue to stay on the offense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will fight the terrorists around the world so we do not have to face them here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll continue to build our alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll never turn over America’s national security needs to leaders of other countries, as we continue to build those alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll continue to spread freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe in the transformational power of liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that the free Iraq is in this nation’s interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe a free Afghanistan is in this nation’s interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe both a free Afghanistan and a free Iraq will serve as a powerful example for millions who plead in silence for liberty in the broader Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done a lot of hard work together over the last three and a half years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been challenged, and we’ve risen to those challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve climbed the mighty mountain.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see the valley below, and it’s a valley of peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: By being steadfast and resolute and strong, by keeping our word, by supporting our troops, we can achieve the peace we all want.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate your listening tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I ask for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And may God continue to bless our great land.
